check_response.text: Tap the person on the shoulder and shout 'Are you OK?' Look, listen and feel for breathing for no more than 10 seconds.

recovery_position.text: The person is breathing. Place them on their side in the recovery position. Keep their airway open and monitor breathing until help arrives.

end_breathing_ok.text: Stay with the person. Call your local emergency number if you have not already done so.

call_help.text: Shout for help. Call your local emergency number now (or ask someone nearby to call). Do not leave the person alone.

start_compressions.text: Place the heel of your hand on the centre of the chest. Place your other hand on top and interlock fingers. Keep arms straight. Push down hard and fast — at least 5 cm (2 inches) deep, at a rate of 100–120 per minute. Give 30 compressions.

trained_rescuer.text: Are you trained in rescue breaths?

rescue_breaths.text: Tilt the head back gently, lift the chin. Pinch the nose shut. Make a normal breath and seal your lips around the person's mouth. Blow for about 1 second and watch the chest rise. Give 2 rescue breaths. Then return immediately to 30 chest compressions.

compressions_only.text: Give continuous chest compressions without rescue breaths. Push hard and fast — 100–120 per minute. Do not stop.

continue_cpr.text: Has help arrived or is the person showing signs of life (breathing, moving)?

keep_going.text: Continue CPR — 30 compressions then 2 rescue breaths (or compressions only). Do not stop unless you are physically unable to continue. Help is on the way.

help_arrived.text: Well done. Hand over to emergency services or follow their instructions. Stay calm.
